verses.text: Some time after this, Naboth from Jezreel owned a vineyard in Jezreel beside the palace of Ahab, king of Samaria.
Ahab told Naboth, “Let me have your vineyard for a vegetable garden. It's right by my house. I'll give you a better vineyard in exchange, or I can pay you what it's worth if you prefer.”
Naboth replied, “May the LORD forbid me from giving you the land I inherited from my ancestors!”
Ahab went home sullen and angry because Naboth from Jezreel had told him, “I won't give you my ancestral land.” Ahab lay down on his bed, turned his face away, and refused to eat.
His wife Jezebel came in and asked, “Why are you so upset that you won't eat?”
He answered, “I offered to buy Naboth's vineyard or give him another one in exchange if he wanted it. He said, ‘I won't give you my vineyard.’”
His wife Jezebel said, “Aren't you the one who rules Israel? Get up, eat something, and cheer up. I'll get you Naboth's vineyard.”
She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth's city.
In the letters she said, “Call a fast and seat Naboth in a prominent place among the people.
Sit two scoundrels opposite him and have them accuse him of cursing God and the king. Then take him out and stone him to death.”
The elders and nobles of the city did exactly what Jezebel told them to do in the letters she sent.
They called a fast and gave Naboth a prominent seat among the people.
The two scoundrels came in and sat across from him. In front of everyone they testified, “Naboth cursed God and the king!” Then the people took him outside the city and stoned him to death.
They sent Jezebel word: “Naboth has been stoned to death.”
When Jezebel heard that Naboth was dead, she told Ahab, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard Naboth from Jezreel refused to sell you. He's dead.”
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to Naboth's vineyard to take possession of it.
Then the LORD gave this message to Elijah the Tishbite:
“Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who lives in Samaria. He's in Naboth's vineyard, where he's gone to take possession of it.

Tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Have you murdered a man and taken his property too?”’ Then tell him, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Where the dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they'll lick up your blood too.”’”
Ahab asked Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?” Elijah replied, “I found you because you've sold yourself to do what's evil in the LORD's sight.
He says, ‘I'll bring disaster on you and sweep you away completely. I'll cut off every male in Ahab's family in Israel, whether shut in or free.
I'll make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you've provoked me to anger and led Israel into sin.’”
The LORD also spoke about Jezebel: “Dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
Dogs will eat anyone from Ahab's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat anyone who dies out in the fields.”
No one sold himself to do what was evil in the LORD's eyes like Ahab did, spurred on by his wife Jezebel.
He did detestable things by following idols, just as the Amorites had done before the LORD drove them out ahead of the Israelites.
When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, dressed in sackcloth, and fasted. He slept in sackcloth and went around dejected.
Then the LORD gave Elijah the Tishbite this message:
“Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself, I won't bring disaster in his lifetime. I'll bring it on his family in his son's time.”
